items.question: How can conceptual cognition grasp reality as it truly is?
premises: Conceptual cognition involves connection with constructs
Connection with constructs mediates apprehension
Mediated apprehension differs from direct grasping
items.inference: Conceptual cognition cannot grasp reality as it truly is
items.plain_english: How can there be a grasping of things as they truly are when cognition is conceptual and bound by associations?

items.question: Can inference ever arise without a previously grasped connection between smoke and fire?
premises: Inference depends on a known invariable connection
The connection between smoke and fire must be grasped beforehand
Without prior grasping no inferential knowledge arises
items.inference: Inference cannot occur without a previously apprehended connection
items.plain_english: Likewise, inference could never arise, since the connection between smoke and fire would never have been grasped.

items.question: Can fire be inferred when the relation between sign and signified remains ungrasped?
premises: Inference requires a grasped relation
If the relation is not grasped it cannot function
Fire is cognized only through such a relation
items.inference: Fire cannot be inferred without a previously grasped relation
items.plain_english: If the relation has not been grasped, it is not grasped; and thus fire cannot be cognized through inference.

items.question: How can a known connection apply to a particular case that is entirely novel?
premises: Inference relies on applying a known connection
A novel particular lacks prior acquaintance
Without prior acquaintance the connection cannot be applied
items.inference: A known connection cannot be established for a wholly novel particular
items.plain_english: And even when a particular case is entirely new, how can there be any connection with what was previously known?

items.question: Can mere smoke by itself constitute a valid instance of inference?
premises: Inference requires more than the mere presence of a sign
Smoke alone lacks the grasped relation to fire
Without that relation inferential status is absent
items.inference: Mere smoke cannot by itself constitute inference
items.plain_english: Nor can there be the status of inference here from smoke alone, taken by itself.

items.question: Why does grasping only one relatum fail to yield inferential knowledge?
premises: Inference rests on two related terms
Grasping only one term omits the relation
Without the relation the inference is not grasped
items.inference: Grasping only one relatum cannot produce inferential knowledge
items.plain_english: Because inference rests on two things, the grasping of only one of them does not amount to grasping that inference.

items.question: What logical defect inevitably arises in the proposed account of inference?
premises: Grasping the relation requires prior inference
Inference requires a prior grasp of the relation
This circularity is difficult to eliminate
items.inference: A mutual fault of circular dependence inevitably arises
items.plain_english: Here, a mutual fault that is hard to avoid inevitably arises.

items.question: Why is apprehension of fire impossible without prior apprehension of its connection?
premises: Apprehension of fire depends on apprehending a connection
Without the connection there is no basis for inference
Therefore fire cannot be apprehended inferentially
items.inference: Apprehension of fire is impossible without apprehension of the connection
items.plain_english: As long as the connection is not apprehended, the apprehension of fire is not possible.

rows.grounds: one who speaks falsely or impossibly

items.question: Why can a source of falsehood never be trusted as a speaker of truth?
premises: Credibility requires consistency in truthfulness
A speaker known for falsehood lacks such consistency
Such a speaker cannot be accepted as truthful
items.inference: A false speaker cannot ever be regarded as a truth speaker
uncertainties: ayovaktā interpreted as a speaker of falsehood or impossibility
items.plain_english: Indeed, one who speaks falsely never shines as a speaker of truth.

items.question: Why does possible untruth in authorities prevent certainty across different contexts?
premises: Even trusted authorities may be untruthful in some cases
Untruthfulness in one context undermines universal reliability
Without universal reliability certainty cannot be established
items.inference: Certainty cannot be secured if authorities may be untruthful elsewhere
items.plain_english: Even a father or others may be untruthful in one case, so there is no certainty that they are truthful elsewhere.

items.question: How does the doctrine of momentariness support the impossibility of stable certainty?
premises: Momentariness entails constant destruction of entities
Constant destruction prevents stable relations over time
Without stable relations certainty cannot be established
items.inference: Reflection on momentariness supports the lack of stable certainty
items.plain_english: This also follows from reflecting on the doctrine of momentary destruction.

items.question: Why does perceptual appearance fail to establish genuine stability for the opponent?
premises: The opponent denies enduring stability
Perception may present things as standing
Apparent standing does not prove real stability
items.inference: Stability is not established even by perception
items.plain_english: For you, stability is not established, even though it appears as standing in perception.

items.question: How can cognition be valid if it is marked by non-correspondence and contradiction?
premises: Valid cognition requires correspondence
Non-correspondence entails contradiction
Contradictory cognition cannot be valid
items.inference: Cognition marked by non-correspondence cannot be valid
items.plain_english: And if it is of the nature of non-correspondence and contradiction, how could it be valid?

items.question: How can one cognizer access another's reflection on momentary destruction?
premises: Momentariness implies no enduring cognizer
Access to another's reflection requires continuity
Without continuity such access is impossible
items.inference: Another's reflection on momentariness cannot be accessed
items.plain_english: Whence could there be access to another person's reflection on momentary destruction?

items.question: How can meaning be grasped from words or sentences under momentariness?
premises: Grasping meaning requires retention across moments
Momentariness denies stable retention
Without retention meaning cannot be grasped from words or sentences
items.inference: Meaning cannot be established from words or sentences
items.plain_english: Likewise, the grasping of meaning from a sentence or from a word is not established.

items.question: How can sequentiality be accounted for in the theory of manifested sphota?
premises: Sphota is proposed as a unitary meaning-bearer
Linguistic apprehension involves sequential sounds
Reconciling unity with sequentiality is problematic
items.inference: Sequentiality remains unexplained in the sphota theory
uncertainties: sphoṭa kept as technical term in grounds
items.plain_english: But even in the view that sphota is manifested, how can there be sequentiality there?

items.question: Why can linguistic entities of mere appearance not be truly grasped?
premises: Linguistic entities are taken as mere appearances
Mere appearances lack stable graspable form
Without stable form grasping cannot occur
items.inference: Linguistic entities of mere appearance cannot be grasped
items.plain_english: There would be no grasping of linguistic things that are of the nature of mere appearance.

rows.grounds: due to the will of the self

items.question: Why cannot sense-organ activity be explained by the will of the self alone?
premises: Sense activity would require control by the self's will
Under the critiqued view no stable controlling self exists
Without a stable controller such activity is unexplained
items.inference: Activity in the sense organs cannot be established by self-will
items.plain_english: Likewise, activity in the group of sense organs cannot be established as arising from the will of the self.

rows.grounds: if there is a single self

items.question: What consequence follows for sense activity if the self is assumed to be one?
premises: If the self is one it should govern all senses uniformly
Uniform governance would imply simultaneous activity everywhere
Such uniformity does not match observed experience
items.inference: Assuming a single self leads to an inappropriate universal activity
items.plain_english: But if there were oneness, then such appropriateness would indeed apply everywhere.

items.question: Can contact with specific senses explain differentiated cognition if the self is one?
premises: Differentiated cognition might be explained by contact with specific senses
This requires contact to produce distinct cognitions
The explanation must account for who becomes the cognizer
items.inference: Contact is proposed as a possible explanation for differentiated cognition
items.plain_english: It might be established through contact, if it occurred through seeing and so on.

items.question: How can one entity become the cognizer when contact arises in another?
premises: Contact arises in a particular sense or locus
Cognizing agency is attributed to another entity
Agency cannot be transferred without explanation
items.inference: Contact in one entity cannot explain cognizing agency in another
items.plain_english: When contact arises in one thing, how can another thing become the cognizer?

items.question: How does the temporal structure of action challenge momentary existence?
premises: An action can be begun, ongoing, and uncompleted
These stages require temporal continuity
Momentary existence denies such continuity
items.inference: The temporal structure of action conflicts with momentariness
items.plain_english: With respect to an action, it may be begun, uncompleted, and ongoing.

items.question: Why does the ordered sequence of causal factors undermine momentary existence?
premises: Action involves factors operating in sequence
Sequence requires persistence across moments
Momentary existence cannot sustain such sequence
items.inference: The sequence of causal factors conflicts with momentariness
items.plain_english: Indeed, there is a sequence of the factors of action in their own respective functions.

items.question: What real object-nature remains if something is merely led by the mind?
premises: If an object is merely led by the mind it lacks independent stability
Independent stability is required for real object-nature
Without it object-nature is questionable
items.inference: A merely mind-led entity lacks genuine object-nature
items.plain_english: If it is led by the mind, what real nature as an object could that have?
